terms.label: Argumentative contribution
terms.definition: A principal explicitly claimed contribution that advances a structured thesis, critique, position, or reasoned argument derived from the review synthesis rather than merely reporting evidence.

terms.label: Benchmark contribution
terms.definition: A principal explicitly claimed contribution that introduces or substantially develops a benchmark, benchmarking protocol, evaluation suite, or comparable standardized resource for comparative evaluation.

terms.label: Conceptual contribution
terms.definition: A principal explicitly claimed contribution consisting of conceptual clarification, synthesis, integration, reframing, or a conceptual model where no more specific controlled contribution type adequately captures the claimed value.

terms.label: Design artifact contribution
terms.definition: A principal explicitly claimed contribution that proposes or develops an engineered/design solution—such as an architecture, prototype, reference design, or design specification—as scholarly value added by the review.

terms.label: Framework contribution
terms.definition: A principal explicitly claimed contribution that introduces, substantially revises, or consolidates an organizing structure of concepts, components, relations, stages, or rules intended to guide analysis, design, evaluation, or understanding.

terms.label: Methodological contribution
terms.definition: A principal explicitly claimed contribution that introduces, adapts, systematizes, or critically develops a method, procedure, protocol, or methodological approach as scholarly value added by the review.

terms.label: Research agenda contribution
terms.definition: A principal explicitly claimed contribution that formulates and organizes multiple future research problems, questions, directions, or priorities into a coherent agenda.

terms.label: Resource contribution
terms.definition: A principal explicitly claimed contribution that provides a reusable research asset—such as a curated dataset, repository, codebase, tool, registry, or structured reference collection—beyond ordinary supplementary material.

terms.label: Taxonomy contribution
terms.definition: A principal explicitly claimed contribution that introduces, substantially revises, or consolidates a structured classification scheme whose categories and organizing distinctions classify phenomena in the reviewed domain.

terms.label: Automated agent
terms.definition: A stage-qualified configuration in which software or an algorithm executes a substantive review task without concurrent substantive human judgment in that execution step, although humans may configure, supervise, or review outputs before/afterward.

terms.label: Hybrid human-machine
terms.definition: A stage-qualified configuration in which human and automated/AI agents make substantively interdependent contributions within the same review task or stage, rather than merely using software as a passive tool.

terms.label: Multiple human reviewers
terms.definition: A workflow stage is performed, checked, duplicated, or resolved by multiple human reviewers/analysts.

terms.label: Single human reviewer
terms.definition: A workflow stage is performed by one human reviewer/analyst.

terms.label: Algorithm
terms.definition: A computational or technical procedure, technique, strategy, or algorithmic approach for transforming inputs or solving a domain task that is itself materially compared, classified, evaluated, or synthesized.

terms.label: Architecture
terms.definition: A system, software, model, or technical architecture treated as a material object of comparison, classification, or synthesis.

terms.label: Benchmark
terms.definition: A benchmark, benchmark suite/task, or dataset functioning as an evaluative reference whose benchmark role, coverage, design, usage, or comparative properties are themselves materially synthesized.

terms.label: Bibliographic metadata
terms.definition: Publication-level metadata (for example year, venue, authorship, citation, keyword, affiliation, or publication counts) that are materially aggregated, modeled, compared, or interpreted across the corpus.

terms.label: Computational model
terms.definition: A computational or machine-learning model family or model instance treated as a material object of comparison, characterization, or synthesis.

terms.label: Concept
terms.definition: A concept, construct, term, or definition that is itself compared, synthesized, clarified, or organized.

terms.label: Dataset
terms.definition: A data collection/corpus whose dataset-level types, properties, availability, distribution, composition, limitations, or use patterns are themselves materially synthesized.

terms.label: Effect estimate
terms.definition: A quantitative effect/performance estimate or comparable normalized quantitative result that is itself extracted, compared, or aggregated across sources.

terms.label: Existing review
terms.definition: A prior review publication whose review-level design, scope, quality, methods, coverage, or conclusions are themselves materially compared/appraised/mapped as review objects.

terms.label: Existing survey
terms.definition: A prior survey publication whose survey-level scope, organization, coverage, methods, or features are directly compared, classified, appraised, or synthesized.

terms.label: Finding
terms.definition: A propositional result, conclusion, qualitative theme, interpretation, or source-level finding that is itself compared/integrated across sources as finding content.

terms.label: Framework
terms.definition: A conceptual, methodological, evaluative, or organizational framework from the reviewed domain that is itself materially compared, classified, mapped, or appraised as an organizing structure.

terms.label: Indicator
terms.definition: A metric, indicator, criterion, index, score, or other operational quantity/dimension that is itself materially compared, categorized, evaluated, or synthesized across the reviewed corpus.

terms.label: Intervention or programme
terms.definition: An intervention, service, programme, policy implementation, or organized practice intervention that is itself compared, characterized, evaluated, or synthesized.

terms.label: Measurement instrument
terms.definition: A scale, questionnaire, rubric, rating system, assessment instrument, or other structured instrument used to generate measurements and itself materially compared, appraised, or synthesized.

terms.label: Mechanism
terms.definition: A causal, explanatory, behavioral, organizational, or realist mechanism that is itself analyzed or synthesized.

terms.label: Practice
terms.definition: A professional, organizational, engineering, clinical, or operational practice that is itself compared, classified, or synthesized.

terms.label: Repository
terms.definition: A repository, archive, registry, or comparable collection service that is itself compared, characterized, or evaluated.

terms.label: Research method
terms.definition: A method for conducting research, evaluation, measurement, evidence synthesis, or empirical investigation that is itself materially compared, classified, appraised, or synthesized. It does not include domain technical/computational techniques merely because authors call them methods or approaches.

terms.label: Research tradition
terms.definition: A distinct research tradition, paradigm, school, or lineage that is itself compared or synthesized.

terms.label: Software tool
terms.definition: Executable software, toolkit, library, platform, package, application, or operational software framework that is itself materially compared, classified, evaluated, or synthesized.

terms.label: Standard
terms.definition: A technical, methodological, professional, reporting, or regulatory standard whose requirements/content/structure are themselves materially compared, mapped, appraised, or synthesized.

terms.label: Study
terms.definition: A primary study treated as an analytical carrier/object whose study-level design, setting, quality, methodology, population, distribution, or other study-level characteristics are themselves materially synthesized.

terms.label: Taxonomy
terms.definition: A taxonomy or classification scheme from the reviewed literature that is itself compared, evaluated, mapped, or synthesized.

terms.label: Theory
terms.definition: A theory or theoretical model that is itself compared, evaluated, synthesized, or mapped.

terms.label: Academic and grey literature corpus
terms.definition: An evidence corpus containing both academic literature and substantively included grey/practice literature.

terms.label: Academic literature corpus
terms.definition: An evidence corpus composed of academic/scholarly literature under the review's inclusion and analysis rules.

terms.label: Grey literature corpus
terms.definition: An evidence corpus composed of grey/practice/non-formally-published literature under the review's inclusion and analysis rules.

terms.label: Existing survey
terms.definition: An included source whose semantic role is an existing survey publication that is itself analyzed by the current review/survey.

terms.label: Methodological guidance source
terms.definition: An included source whose evidential role is to provide methodological knowledge, guidance, recommendations, reporting/conduct guidance, or method-focused evidence about how research, reviews, evidence synthesis, appraisal, measurement, or reporting should be designed or performed, where that methodological content materially contributes to the review synthesis.

terms.label: Practice-based source
terms.definition: An included source whose evidential role is to contribute practitioner, professional, operational, organizational, policy/practice, or other practice-origin knowledge/data substantively to the synthesis, regardless of document format.

terms.label: Primary study report
terms.definition: An included source whose semantic role is to report original primary research that contributes analyzable evidence to the review.

terms.label: Secondary study report
terms.definition: An included source whose semantic role is to report a prior secondary synthesis such as a review or meta-analysis.

terms.label: Rapid execution mode
terms.definition: A process modifier indicating that the review deliberately uses an accelerated or rapid review approach.

terms.label: Cross-layer lens
terms.definition: An organizing lens in which the review explicitly defines at least two distinct layers/levels of a system or phenomenon and materially synthesizes relationships between them—such as dependencies, interfaces, propagation, feedback, trade-offs, or co-design—rather than merely covering multiple components, axes, or phases.

terms.label: Agenda-setting function
terms.definition: A principal publication function that explicitly structures, prioritizes, or formulates multiple future research directions or questions as a major purpose of the publication.

terms.label: Critical synthesis function
terms.definition: A principal publication function explicitly aimed at interpretive critique of assumptions, contradictions, limitations, validity, paradigms, or applicability across the literature.

terms.label: Perspective function
terms.definition: A principal publication function that explicitly offers a perspective or interpretive viewpoint on a field rather than only summarizing evidence.

terms.label: Position function
terms.definition: A principal publication function that explicitly advances or defends a scholarly position, stance, or normative claim.

terms.label: Protocol function
terms.definition: A principal publication function that presents the planned methods or protocol for a review or synthesis before or independently of reporting completed review findings.

terms.label: State-of-the-art function
terms.definition: A principal publication function whose explicit objective is to characterize the current state, current landscape, or current research frontier of a field at a defined time and which materially realizes that temporal/current-state characterization.

terms.label: Survey function
terms.definition: A principal publication function that explicitly presents the article as a survey or field-organizing survey and materially realizes that role.

terms.label: Tutorial function
terms.definition: A principal publication function that explicitly teaches or explains a field, method, or body of concepts to enable reader understanding or practice.

terms.label: Vision function
terms.definition: A principal publication function that explicitly articulates a desired or anticipated future state, architecture, principles, or development trajectory for a field and substantively develops that future-oriented view.

terms.label: Explicitly not registered
terms.definition: The publication explicitly states that the review was not registered.

terms.label: Registered
terms.definition: The review investigation is explicitly registered in a review registry or comparable formal registration system.

terms.label: Integrative review design
terms.definition: A review design explicitly using an integrative review approach to combine heterogeneous forms of literature or evidence within one review design.

terms.label: Meta-narrative review design
terms.definition: A review design explicitly using meta-narrative methodology to examine how different research traditions have conceptualized and studied a topic.

terms.label: Narrative review design
terms.definition: A review design explicitly presented as a narrative review or clearly organized as an author-led narrative review design rather than merely using narrative prose for synthesis.

terms.label: Qualitative evidence synthesis design
terms.definition: A review design whose primary methodological design is synthesis of qualitative evidence or qualitative findings.

terms.label: Realist review design
terms.definition: A review design explicitly using realist review methodology to explain how and why outcomes arise in contexts through mechanisms or comparable realist constructs.

terms.label: Scoping review design
terms.definition: A review design explicitly conducted as a scoping review to map the extent, characteristics, concepts, or evidence landscape of a field.

terms.label: Systematic mapping design
terms.definition: A review design whose declared methodological purpose is systematic mapping/classification of a research area using an explicit systematic study-selection process.

terms.label: Systematic review design
terms.definition: A review design in which the publication frames the review itself as systematic and realizes that framing through an explicit, structured/reproducible evidence search or retrieval process plus explicit screening/selection/eligibility decisions for a bounded evidence set.

terms.label: Systematized review design
terms.definition: A review design explicitly presented as systematized/systematised or semi-systematic: it deliberately applies substantial systematic-review elements while not claiming, or not meeting the publication’s own claim of, a full systematic review design.

terms.label: Umbrella review design
terms.definition: A review-of-reviews design in which existing systematic reviews or comparable secondary syntheses are the principal evidence units.

terms.label: Blog post
terms.definition: A blog or web-post publication used as an included source.

terms.label: Book or chapter
terms.definition: A book or book chapter used as an included source.

terms.label: Conference paper
terms.definition: A paper published in or as part of a scholarly conference/proceedings venue.

terms.label: Documentation
terms.definition: Technical, software, platform, API, or other formal documentation used as an included source.

terms.label: Editorial or commentary
terms.definition: An editorial, commentary, viewpoint, or comparable short opinion/interpretive publication used as an included source.

terms.label: Guideline
terms.definition: A formal guideline or recommendations document used as an included source.

terms.label: Journal article
terms.definition: A scholarly article published in a journal.

terms.label: Preprint
terms.definition: A manuscript publicly disseminated before or without formal version-of-record publication.

terms.label: Programme manual
terms.definition: A manual describing the operation, delivery, or procedures of a programme/intervention used as an included source.

terms.label: Standard
terms.definition: A formal technical, professional, or regulatory standard used as an included source.

terms.label: Technical report
terms.definition: A formal technical or research report issued outside ordinary journal/conference publication.

terms.label: Thesis
terms.definition: A dissertation or thesis submitted for an academic degree.

terms.label: White paper
terms.definition: An authoritative or policy/industry-oriented white paper used as an included source.

terms.label: Living update mode
terms.definition: A process modifier indicating an intentionally ongoing review that is planned to be updated as new evidence becomes available.

terms.label: Benchmark artifact
terms.definition: A discrete reusable benchmark, evaluation suite, benchmarking protocol, or reference resource produced by the review to support standardized comparison or evaluation.

terms.label: Conceptual model artifact
terms.definition: A discrete conceptual model produced by the review that represents concepts/entities and meaningful relationships among them; a simple list or category table is insufficient.

terms.label: Design artifact
terms.definition: A discrete engineered or design-oriented output produced by the review, such as an architecture, prototype, reference design, design specification, or comparable solution with identity beyond descriptive analysis.

terms.label: Evidence map
terms.definition: A discrete structured representation of the distribution of evidence across defined dimensions or questions, intended to show coverage, concentration, and/or gaps; an ordinary results table is insufficient.

terms.label: Framework artifact
terms.definition: A discrete, identifiable organizing or analytical framework produced by the review, with defined components/relations/rules that can be independently referred to or reused beyond an ordinary summary table.

terms.label: Research agenda
terms.definition: A discrete structured output that organizes multiple future research questions, problems, directions, or priorities into an identifiable agenda rather than a generic future-work paragraph.

terms.label: Research resource
terms.definition: A discrete reusable research asset produced or released with the review, such as a curated dataset, codebase, repository, tool, registry, or structured reference collection that has identity beyond ordinary supplementary material.

terms.label: Taxonomy artifact
terms.definition: A discrete classification scheme produced by the review that organizes domain entities or concepts into named categories using explicit distinctions, dimensions, or assignment principles.

terms.label: Bibliometric/network synthesis
terms.definition: A substantive bibliometric/scientometric or network synthesis that integrates publication/citation/co-authorship/co-word or related metadata to characterize corpus-level structure, relationships, or trends; routine publication counts alone are insufficient.

terms.label: Descriptive mapping synthesis
terms.definition: A substantive synthesis method that systematically maps the included evidence across explicit categories, dimensions, or cells and interprets corpus-level distributions, patterns, concentrations, or gaps produced by that mapping.

terms.label: Framework synthesis
terms.definition: A synthesis method that systematically codes, organizes, maps, or interprets evidence across sources through an explicit analytical/a priori framework.

terms.label: Meta-analysis
terms.definition: A quantitative synthesis method that statistically combines effect estimates or comparable quantitative results across studies.

terms.label: Meta-narrative synthesis
terms.definition: A synthesis method that compares and integrates the narratives, paradigms, or trajectories of distinct research traditions.

terms.label: Mixed-methods synthesis
terms.definition: A synthesis method that explicitly integrates quantitative and qualitative evidence or synthesis components within one mixed-methods synthesis.

terms.label: Narrative synthesis
terms.definition: A substantive synthesis method that integrates evidence across sources through a deliberate narrative procedure. An explicit narrative-synthesis statement plus a described cross-source organization/integration step is sufficient; narrative prose alone is not.

terms.label: Qualitative content analysis
terms.definition: A synthesis method using explicit qualitative content-analysis procedures to code and interpret textual material across the evidence corpus.

terms.label: Qualitative meta-synthesis
terms.definition: A qualitative synthesis method explicitly described as qualitative meta-synthesis or an equivalent meta-synthetic procedure.

terms.label: Realist synthesis
terms.definition: A synthesis method that explains how outcomes arise through mechanisms in contexts using realist synthesis logic.

terms.label: Thematic synthesis
terms.definition: A synthesis method that develops or synthesizes themes across qualitative or textual evidence.

inference_rules: NONE: no inferred subtypes, equivalences, disjointness or closed-world negatives
